title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is not a manuscript note. It is a typed page numbered 28, with handwritten fill-ins, from the 1960s étale-cohomology seminar text. By its content it matches the relative cohomological purity section of SGA 4, Exposé XVI (Artin, 'Théorème de changement de base par un morphisme lisse, et applications'), §3. Its internal references (3.2, 3.4, 3.5, VI 4.5, XII 6.5) and its use of 'ind L-groupes' fit that section. The page has been filed among the 'Cristaux / gribouillis' material, and the next page (motivic realisations) is unrelated.

Setting: f: X→S is smooth and Y⊂X is a closed subscheme with Y smooth over S, so (Y,X) is a smooth S-pair of constant codimension c. Let j: U = X−Y → X be the open immersion and g = f∘j. F is a sheaf on S of ind-L-groups, with L a set of primes invertible on S.

The statement being proved is that the formation of R^q j_*(g^*F) commutes with arbitrary base change u: S'→S. That is, the base-change map u'^*(R^q j_*)g^*F → (R^q j'_*)g'^*u^*F is an isomorphism, where u' = u×_S X. For nonabelian F only q = 0, 1 make sense. For abelian sheaves, the last assertion of the theorem is equivalent to the first by VI 4.5.

Step q = 0: by (3.2), f^*F → j_*g^*F is an isomorphism, because Y has codimension ≥1 and the fibres are normal. Applying this both before and after base change, together with u'^*f^* = f'^*u^*, gives the commutative square of isomorphisms shown on the page.

Step q > 0: by the usual limit argument one reduces to S, X, Y of finite type over Spec Z. One may then take S' to be a geometric point s̄ of S (XII 6.5).

If c ≠ 1, purity in low degree (3.4) gives R^q j_* g^*F = 0 both before and after base change, which settles that case.

If c = 1, one takes a geometric point x̄ of X over s̄ lying in Y. One then computes the stalk with the local model of (3.5): strict henselisation, a tame Kummer cover along the divisor Y, and R^1 j_* given by a Tate-twisted F. That computation is visibly compatible with passage to the fibre; the page breaks off at the start of it.

The pencilled margin note, apparently 'démonstration peu naturelle', looks like a reader's (probably Grothendieck's) critical comment on the proof's style.
errors: No mathematical errors are visible. The argument is standard and is cut off at the start of the codimension-1 case.

ideas.what: Base-change compatibility of R^q j_* g^*F for the complement of a smooth relative divisor/subscheme in a smooth S-scheme (relative cohomological purity), including nonabelian ind-L-group coefficients
ideas.modern_name: Relative cohomological purity for smooth pairs / tame ramification along a relative smooth divisor; base change for R^q j_*
ideas.usually_credited_to: M. Artin / Grothendieck, SGA 4 Exp. XVI §3 (and XIX for absolute purity in equal characteristic)

ideas.what: Reduction to finite type over Z and to base change to a geometric point
ideas.modern_name: Standard limit argument and pointwise criterion for base change

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typed page from the published SGA 4 Exposé XVI proof of base change for relative purity. The only unpublished trace is a short pencilled marginal comment.
transcription_corrections: The handwritten marginal note is more plausibly 'démonstration peu naturelle' than 'démonstration par notre vieille'.
The page is typescript (page 28 of an SGA 4 XVI draft) with manuscript insertions 'VI 4.5', 'XII 6.5' and '3.4'; the struck-out typed words are illegible overstrikes.
The archive stamp '69' in the lower-left corner is the archive folio number, not part of the text.
